recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5185 unless PA reopens a broader, separate infrastructure question about cross-resource equivalence.
issue_request: FHIR-5185 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification PA change request from the January 2015 ballot for FHIR-core Person and RelatedPerson. The balloter questioned whether Person was an inappropriate one-off mechanism for linking equivalent resources across servers, and the final resolution was to update the Person notes to better describe how Person linkages work and the use cases supporting the resource.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied in git commit dc2afae9f6e31b220e90a9d948c46e3743363e68, whose subject explicitly lists tracker 5185 among grouped Person ballot reconciliation changes. That commit revised the Person introduction, added concrete Person.link Patient and RelatedPerson entries to the Person example, and replaced the old PA notes with Person linking/use-case narrative including cross-domain directories and a client portal use case.
additional_context: Person and RelatedPerson are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. Current source/person/person-introduction.xml describes Person as a linkage resource for common demographics across Patient, Practitioner, and RelatedPerson records and explains direct and indirect linkage through FHIR resources or business identifiers. Current source/person/person-notes.xml contains the Person and Linking section plus Cross-Domain Patient Directory, Cross-Domain Provider Directory, Person Master Index, Client Portal, and Security and Privacy Considerations sections. Later Published issues FHIR-17399 and FHIR-20485 refined nearby Person linking and PMI wording without reversing the FHIR-5185 decision, and related grouped Person ballot issues have already been audited on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative Person source already answers the ballot concern by explaining the supported linkage scenarios and use cases, and adding more general resource-equivalence infrastructure or duplicative prose would go beyond the accepted FHIR-5185 resolution.
